decisions.reason: Despite strong relatedness to our crate know-how, its crop-specific niche and disappearance from view after the launch phase suggest that learning has not translated into a scalable portfolio position, so we would reallocate resources.

A stackable plastic crate is deeply embedded in our existing packaging capabilities, and weak standalone visibility is more likely to reflect integration into the broader offer than a lack of absorptive potential.
This rackable pallet line remains close to our core pallet engineering and manufacturing base, giving us ample ability to refine it commercially rather than withdraw it.

The spill-retention pallet is adjacent but more specialized, and after the initial dedicated launch its later absence suggests limited market learning and weaker justification for continued resource commitment.
As a variant on our established plastic pallet platform, it still benefits from strong internal knowledge and can be sustained as an incremental offering even if it is no longer prominently marketed.
